lines.text: Do you know how elevator safety works? It's not one trick. It's several, stacked on top of each other.
First, it hangs from several steel cables, usually four or more. Any one of them can hold the car on its own.
On the other end is a heavy counterweight, about the weight of the car plus half a full load. So the motor barely lifts anything. It just tips the balance.
At the top sits a speed limiter called a governor. If the car ever goes too fast, it trips the safety brakes.
Steel wedges grab the guide rails, and squeeze the car to a stop.
In 1854, Elisha Otis stood on a raised platform in New York, and had the rope cut. The brake caught him. That's what made tall buildings practical.
And at the very bottom of the shaft, big springs or oil buffers wait, just in case.
So an elevator never trusts one cable. It trusts a whole stack of backups.
